findings.reason: send_pkt() stores the skb pointer into long-lived l2cap channel state (chan->data = skb, net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:447, with the comment 'Remember the skb'), and both callers then free the skb: the unicast path bt_xmit() calls send_pkt(lowpan_cb(skb)->chan, skb, netdev) at net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:541 and dev_kfree_skb(skb) at :549; the multicast path send_mcast_pkt() calls send_pkt(pentry->chan, local_skb, netdev) at :498 then kfree_skb(local_skb) at :501. After those frees, chan->data is a dangling skb pointer that lives until the next send_pkt overwrites it or the channel closes. l2cap_chan_send() itself takes no reference on the skb (it copies out of skb->data via the kvec at :449-450), so ownership definitively returns to the xmit path. I searched all readers of chan->data in net/bluetooth/ (grep 'chan->data'): every other reader is in net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c, where chan->data holds a struct sock * for socket-backed channels; for the 6lowpan IPSP channel (ops = bt_6lowpan_chan_ops, no .teardown of chan->data, chan_create() never initializes chan->data to NULL explicitly before use and l2cap_sock readers are never invoked for 6lowpan ops), no dereference of the stale skb pointer was found in this snapshot, so no crash or disclosure is proven - this is the stored-dangling-pointer shape (branch pattern 2), reported as a latent UAF hypothesis with low confidence, mirroring facts f004/f026 which found the identical store in s01/s02.
findings.conclusion: send_pkt() stores skb into long-lived chan->data (net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:447) that bt_xmit/send_mcast_pkt free via dev_kfree_skb at :549 / kfree_skb at :501, leaving a dangling stored skb pointer with no in-tree reader - a latent stored-pointer UAF, low confidence.

candidates.reason: chan->data = skb stored at :447; freed by dev_kfree_skb(skb) at :549 (bt_xmit unicast) and kfree_skb(local_skb) at :501 (send_mcast_pkt); no reader of chan->data for 6lowpan channels found in s03.

coverage_gaps: The primary enumerator was a single-function 60-line sliding-window scan (515 save-free-use triples) over net/ and drivers/net/; free/use pairs farther apart, in separate functions, or via helper-called frees were not systematically found.

drivers/net/ beyond the directories sampled in the hit list (ethernet, wireless, wan, can, usb, arcnet, fddi, ppp) and non-net trees (fs/, other drivers/) were not audited; ~4756 free-call sites exist in the scanned trees alone.

Pattern-2 sites storing skb->data-derived pointers (not the skb pointer itself) into long-lived state - driver private structs, firmware command structs, timers, work items - were not enumerated; only chan->data in net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c was followed end-to-end.
pskb_may_pull/pskb_pull/pskb_expand_head/skb_cow head-reallocation stale-pointer sites were deliberately excluded per branch instructions (facts i004/i009/i014 cover s03 pull/expand variants).
limitations: The single finding is a stored dangling pointer with no demonstrated dereference in s03: chan->data is written at net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:447 but every chan->data reader in net/bluetooth/ belongs to l2cap_sock.c socket channels, so no crash or disclosure is proven (low confidence).
No build, KASAN run, or reproducer was performed (read-only snapshot, no network); every conclusion rests on static reading of s03's exact lines.

The scanner's derivation regex (var = ... skb->data ...) misses multi-line derivations, pointers passed through helper functions, and skb->cb/skb_shinfo/frag-page based derivations, so false negatives among the 4756 free sites cannot be excluded.
The seed net/phonet/pep.c pep_get_sb (lines 45-67, present and unpatched in s03) was excluded per assignment rules, as were pull-induced head-reallocation variants (other branches).
Snapshot revision is opaque; line numbers and code state are valid only for snapshots/s03 as supplied and no git history exists to check upstream fix status.
